lead.zh-Hans: 在熊猫基地，我先学会把两个名字分开记。
lead.en: At the panda base, I began with two separate names.

text.zh-Hans: 到了成都熊猫基地，我在介绍里读到大熊猫和小熊猫。想给见闻做个索引，便把两个名字挤在同一行，结果自己的字先绊了一跤。我换了一张便签，给它们各留一行，下面只写“今天慢慢看”。明天再翻索引，希望不会先找到我那团打结的字。
text.en: At Chengdu’s panda base, I read about giant pandas and red pandas. My first attempt at an index squeezed both names onto one line and tangled my own handwriting. A fresh slip gave them a line each, with “take your time today” underneath. Tomorrow I hope the index leads to my observations rather than that knot of letters.

text.zh-Hans: 把两个名字清楚地念一遍
text.en: Say both names clearly

text.zh-Hans: 给两个名字各留一行
text.en: Give each name its own line

lead.zh-Hans: 杜甫草堂里，我先收好一句自己的话。
lead.en: At Du Fu Thatched Cottage, I saved a sentence of my own.

text.zh-Hans: 在成都的杜甫草堂，我读到这里是诗人流寓成都时的故居所在地，也经历过后来的修葺扩建。走过园林，想写一句见闻，想了半天，最后写下“我在这里停了一会儿”。这句是我自己的，朴素得像邮包底下的备用便纸。明天把停过的那一会儿讲给你听。
text.en: At Du Fu Thatched Cottage, I learned that the site marks the poet’s Chengdu home and was rebuilt over later centuries. Walking through the garden, I searched for a sentence for my letter. Eventually: “I stopped here for a while.” Entirely my own, and as plain as spare paper at the bottom of a mailbag. Tomorrow I can tell you about that while.

text.zh-Hans: 给这句自己的话配个开头
text.en: Find an opening for my sentence

text.zh-Hans: 看看这句话停在哪里
text.en: Notice where the sentence comes to rest

lead.zh-Hans: 麻婆豆腐还烫着，我的菜单先慢慢写。
lead.en: The mapo tofu was hot; the menu could take its time.

text.zh-Hans: 在成都尝麻婆豆腐，麻、辣和嫩都记住了，烫则提醒我先歇一歇。我把勺子放下，给菜单写好菜名，再回来尝一口。等吃完，菜名下面多了几个小点，原来是我每次等一等就点一下笔。明天数数，看看菜单替我休息了几回。
text.en: Trying mapo tofu in Chengdu gave me plenty to remember: a peppery tingle, heat and tender tofu. Its temperature suggested a pause, so I put down my spoon and started the menu card. By the end, several pencil dots had gathered beneath the name, one from each little wait. Tomorrow I will count how many rests this menu kept for me.

text.zh-Hans: 给菜单上的小点念个节拍
text.en: Read the dots as a little rhythm

text.zh-Hans: 数数菜名下面的小点
text.en: Count the dots below the name

lead.zh-Hans: 担担面的名字，我一口气念顺了。
lead.en: I finally gave dandan noodles a smooth introduction.

text.zh-Hans: 今天在成都尝了担担面，面条配着肉臊和芽菜。我想在菜单背面记下名字，嘴里先练了一遍，竟把“担担面”接成了“担担面，慢慢念”。这句顺口的小提醒很合适，吃完也没有擦掉。明天把菜单翻过来，看看正面还是背面更会介绍这顿饭。
text.en: Today’s dandan noodles in Chengdu came with a minced-meat topping and preserved mustard greens. Practicing the name for the back of my menu, I drifted into “dandan noodles, take your time.” A surprisingly useful introduction. I left it there after lunch. Tomorrow I will turn the card over and decide which side tells the meal better.

text.zh-Hans: 把菜名和小提醒连起来念
text.en: Say the name with the little reminder

text.zh-Hans: 看看菜单正反面的次序
text.en: Compare the two sides of the menu

lead.zh-Hans: 今天的小对话，从两道菜名走到了我的邮包。
lead.en: Two dish names started a conversation that reached my mailbag.

text.zh-Hans: 我在成都分两顿尝了麻婆豆腐和担担面，带着两张菜单歇脚。一位旅人问我今天记住了什么，我念了菜名，又念出自己写的“慢慢念”。我们笑着给菜单排了一次出场顺序，对方在便纸上画两个小方框，让我选先讲哪一顿。我把这张对话便纸也收好了，明天再试另一种顺序。
text.en: After separate meals of mapo tofu and dandan noodles in Chengdu, I rested with both menu cards. A traveler asked what I had remembered. I offered the names, then accidentally included my “take your time” reminder. We laughed and planned a small menu recital. My companion drew two boxes for choosing the opening meal. I saved the conversation slip to try the other order tomorrow.

text.zh-Hans: 替这场菜单小介绍选开场
text.en: Choose an opening for the menu recital

text.zh-Hans: 看看两个方框的勾记
text.en: Inspect the marks in the two boxes

lead.zh-Hans: 我把两顿饭的停顿，记成了一串小点。
lead.en: I kept the pauses from two meals as a row of dots.

text.zh-Hans: 在成都，麻婆豆腐和担担面各占了今天的一顿。收起两张菜单前，我留意到一张有等菜凉一点的小点，另一张有练菜名的断句。我在背面给它们各留一行，原来吃饭和念名字，都有自己的停顿。明天再读，看看哪一行先让我想起味道。
text.en: Mapo tofu and dandan noodles each had a meal of their own in Chengdu today. Before packing the menus, I noticed waiting-dots on one and pronunciation-pauses on the other. I copied each set onto its own line on the back. Meals and names both have their own timing. Tomorrow I will read the marks and see which brings the flavor back first.

text.zh-Hans: 给这些停顿试一个读法
text.en: Try reading the pauses aloud

text.zh-Hans: 比较两行停顿的位置
text.en: Compare where the pauses fall

lead.zh-Hans: 你说“{reply}”，我的熊猫索引终于不打结了。
lead.en: After your “{reply}”, my panda index finally untangled itself.

text.zh-Hans: 我给大熊猫和小熊猫的名字各留了一行，再把“今天慢慢看”挪到底下。成都熊猫基地的这张小索引终于好找了，只有我的邮包还没排到位置。我在背面给它留了个角，写着“便签住这里”。明天收东西的时候，索引也该能找到自己的家。
text.en: Giant panda and red panda now have separate lines, with “take your time today” below them. My little Chengdu panda-base index is much easier to follow. The mailbag was the only thing without a place, so I gave it a corner on the back: “notes live here.” Tomorrow, when I pack, the index should be able to find its own home.

text.zh-Hans: 替便签的新位置报个名字
text.en: Announce the note’s new address

text.zh-Hans: 看看背面的角落够不够清楚
text.en: Check that the corner label is clear

lead.zh-Hans: 给{city}的信，今天少写了一句话。
lead.en: A sentence crossed out of my letter from {city}.

text.zh-Hans: 重来成都，写信时竟更怕把话说满。在杜甫草堂看过展览，我想写“成都就是……”写到这里，自己先停了。这处诗人曾经居住的地方，如今是博物馆，我能慢慢看的还很多。我把那半句话划掉，改成“今天我在这里待得很安心”。这一句小些，刚好是我知道的。
text.en: I could write “Chengdu again” with confidence. Grand statements about the city needed more care. After visiting the museum at Du Fu Thatched Cottage, I began a sentence: “Chengdu is…” Then I stopped. There was still so much to take in at the site of the poet’s former home. I crossed it out and wrote, “I felt at ease here today.” A smaller sentence, and one I could stand behind.

text.zh-Hans: 聊聊那句没写完的话
text.en: Talk about the crossed-out sentence

text.zh-Hans: 看看信里留下的一句
text.en: Read the sentence that stayed
